The world

TETRAA single world · A thousand stories

One world turning on the four-sided die, all four faces charted and mapped.

Water
At least half of every face
Edges
Land and sea continue across every edge
Size
20,000 miles from the corner of Spikia, straight through the world, to the base of Mount Celestial. Worked out from that, not yet Ruby’s word: about 24,500 miles along each edge.

The calendar

Months
13 · 28 days each. Counted Ruby’s way, from March, September, October, November and December are the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th months and Tredesember the 13th; the strip below runs that way, with January, February and Tredesember at its end, after the Restart Day.
Year
364 days + the Restart Day, which is one and a quarter days long: 365¼ days, so there are no leap years. The year begins on 1 January. The Restart Day closes it, between December and the next January, and the rain comes with it; on the strip, New Year comes round in the middle, sort of, as Ruby puts it.
Week
7 days: Starday, Moonday, Goldday, Blueday, Spikeday, Wetday, Twilightday. A month is exactly four weeks. That the year begins on a Starday and the Restart Day stands outside the week, so that every month runs from a Starday to a Twilightday, is a reading, not yet Ruby’s word.
One day
One full turn · 25 hours
Spin
Leftward
Years
Counted from year 0. There is a year -0 as well, and it is not the same year as 0. The years before run backwards, the way BCE does on Earth.
Now
Year 1750 (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “the year has advannced to 1750 on tetra”; it was 1700 on 2026-10-14, “the current year is 1700”). In technology, about Earth’s 1750, as she said when the year was 1700.
The weekAs proposed and accepted: Starday for the star, Moonday for the d3 moon, Goldday for the magical field whose light flows like gold, Blueday for the magnetic field, Spikeday for Spikia, Wetday for Wetia, Twilightday for Mount Celestial.

Seasons on the Canon Face · on average

    A slower turn, a richer world.

    The two fields

    Magical field · slows lightGoes all the way around the world. It slows light, so dawn crosses the land slowly and the first light comes in gold, and it turns the dark purple star’s light into the colour of our own sunlight.Here, the morning moves slower. And light flows like gold.
    Magnetic field · guides worldsGoes all the way around the world too. It guides worlds.

    The star

    A dark purple starTetra’s sun is a dark purple star. Its light reaches the ground the colour of our own sun’s light, because the magical field turns it on the way in. It stays level with the middle of the world, never higher and never lower, so every place has as much bright as dark, and on Mount Celestial it sits on the horizon all year.

    The moon

    A d3 moonTetra’s moon is a three-sided die, a d3, and not the cube kind: one crater on its one side, two craters on its two side, three craters on its three side. It is a fair die (Ruby: “a fair d3 for tetra”) and not a barrel (Ruby, 2026-10-11: “Remake the moons without the “barrel” method”): a chunky rounded three-sided pebble, a little longer than it is wide, with domed ends too steep to balance on, so it can only ever come to rest on one of its three sides. Which non-barrel shape to use was a reading. It is a third of the size of Tetra, circles a little farther out than the magical field, and rolls slowly so every side comes round. Every ordinary day it sits on the opposite side from the star, drifting gently about that spot. Every month, in the middle of the month, is the new moon: the die swings round in front of the star and the world goes dark, a solar eclipse. Its light waxes and wanes through the month like our own moon’s, full when the month turns, and the Restart Day is never a new moon. While the die covers the star, every place on Tetra reads “Eclipse”, day side and night side alike.

    The four faces

      The Dice System

      Worlds beyond chance. Tetra is the four-sided world, Hexa the cube planet and Octa the eight-sided planet; they share this page, and the buttons under the title switch between them. Every other planet shows in each world’s sky (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “you shuld be able to see all of the other planets from a given planet”): the built ones as small turning dice, the five not yet built as points of light with their names, on one curved line from the star that runs through this world (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “Why are all the planets not in a curved line from te sun”, then: it “was including the planet you are on”, then: “make them in a fixed pint in space that lets it look like they are actualy all in a line and not you are just zoomed in on one planet, engulfing he rest in its fields”), in the order she stacked the fields (“going away from the star would be the direction they were stacked in”): the planets nearer the star stand between it and this world on the screen, the farther ones carry the line on past it. They stand at fixed places in space along that line, outside this world’s fields, so turning and zooming out (the zoom now goes far enough) shows the whole row as it is; a planet hides behind this world or the moon only when it is farther away than they are. The spacing and the bend are readings. She placed only Tetra first and Hexa last; the page sorts the rest by die size, which puts Octa and the five beyond Hexa: a reading she may overrule. The line’s bend and where it runs across the sky are readings.

        Different worlds. Same imagination.

        Life of Tetra

        The Umbrella Tree Zinnia

        A single tall stem that is not wood, crowned with a wide umbrella of broad petals. Small blossoms hang on threads from the rim of the crown.

        It grows in magical places with a lot of water, most of all in Wetia and on the West Face.

        There are more of them on Hexa than here, since there is more magic there (Ruby).

        Ruby: “add most of the recognizable plants from the real world to bouth”. So most of the plants you would know from Earth grow on Tetra too, for example oaks, pines, birches, maples, willows, palms, bamboo, cactuses, ferns, mosses, grasses, clover, dandelions, daisies, roses, sunflowers, lilies, lotuses, wheat, corn, rice, apple trees, cherry trees, orange trees and strawberries. Which grows where is unwritten. Ruby: “anything that grows on tetra also grows on cuba”, so all of these grow on Hexa too.

              The world

              HEXAThe cube planet · The Dice System

              A world with six square sides, the second world of Ruby’s Dice System after Tetra.

              Sides
              Six, named like Tetra’s with two more: Canon, East, West, Far, North and South. North is the top and South the bottom. Looking at Canon, East is on its left, West on its right and Far behind it.
              Drawn so far
              The Canon side: the Plus Continent, whose four arms reach the sides and connect onto the East, West, North and South sides, with the Canyon in its middle, the small hole that takes you through the world to the Far side. The Far side, from Ruby’s words of 2026-10-05, “the far side has a main island about a quarter of the sise of the face with land on the north east and south east corners, making it half water. on the central island, north of the canyon, there is a volcano (active) (shoots lava every reset day)”: the main island around the Canyon’s other end, land on the north-east and south-east corners, half water, and the volcano north of the Canyon, erupting every Restart Day. The North, East, South and West sides (2026-10-06): drawn from Ruby’s sketches of the explorers’ maps (Aquamarine, Axinite, Benitoite, Chrysoberyl), with the Plus Continent’s arms reaching in as far as the sketches show, and since 2026-10-10 the two portals in the sea on North and West (Ruby: “The rings that were drawn as “islands” were actualy portals. No crescent land, bouth spiral islands are portals in the ocean.”). Nothing on those four sides has a name, and none is coming (Ruby, 2026-10-14: “humands didn't develop there, they don't have any”). All of it is drawn smaller since 2026-10-17, the same shapes at seven tenths (Ruby: “just shrink them”).
              Water
              Ruby, 2026-10-11: “Hexa is a very very very watery planet”. Asked whether the lands should shrink to match, Ruby said on 2026-10-17: “yes but dont change the shape, just shrink them”. So every land is drawn at seven tenths of its size, the same shape (the Plus Continent’s arms thinner but still reaching the four sides; how much to shrink is a reading, she gave no number), and the sides now measure about seven tenths water on Canon, three quarters on Far, four fifths on North and East, and nineteen twentieths on South and West (before the shrink: three fifths, half, two thirds, and nine tenths or more).
              Names
              None of their own: Ruby, 2026-10-14, “humands didn't develop there, they don't have any”. The Plus Continent and the Canyon are what she called them; what this page calls the rest (the arms, the corner lands, the main island, the volcano, the portals) describes them, it does not name them.
              The name
              Hexa, since Ruby’s line of 2026-10-10: “Hey the hedron name for a cube was a hexahedron So Cuba should be called hexa.” It was Cuba from 2026-10-04 until then.
              Size
              About 20,000 miles from one end of the Canyon to the other, probably: as long as Tetra is from the corner of Spikia through to Mount Celestial (Ruby). The Canyon runs straight through, so that is the length of every edge (a reading).
              Turn
              The same way as Tetra, leftward, and a day the same length as Tetra’s: one full turn, 25 hours.
              The star
              Tetra’s dark purple star, seen from farther out. It stays where it is: turn the world to find it, as Ruby asked.
              The sky
              Tetra is visible as a small four-sided world toward the star (Ruby: “you shuld be able to see tetra from cuba and vice versa”), and since 2026-10-18 every other planet too (“you shuld be able to see all of the other planets from a given planet”): Octa as a small eight-sided die beyond it, the five not yet built as points of light with their names farther along, on one curved line from the star that runs through this world (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “Why are all the planets not in a curved line from te sun”, then: it “was including the planet you are on”, then: “make them in a fixed pint in space that lets it look like they are actualy all in a line and not you are just zoomed in on one planet, engulfing he rest in its fields”), in the order she stacked the fields (“going away from the star would be the direction they were stacked in”): the planets nearer the star stand between it and this world on the screen, the farther ones carry the line on past it. They stand at fixed places in space along that line, outside this world’s fields, so turning and zooming out (the zoom now goes far enough) shows the whole row as it is; a planet hides behind this world or the moon only when it is farther away than they are. The spacing and the bend are readings. She placed only Tetra first and Hexa last; the page sorts the rest by die size, which puts Octa and the five beyond Hexa: a reading she may overrule. The line’s bend and where it runs across the sky are readings.
              Fields
              One magical and one magnetic, both a little stronger than Tetra’s (Ruby): the gold and blue rings around the world, hidden only where the world itself is in front of them.
              Place
              Farther from the star than Tetra. Ruby: “if there were 5 magical fields, and tetra was in the first one, cuba would be in the last one (going away from the star would be the direction they were stacked in)”.

              The calendar

              Months
              14 · 28 days each: Tetra’s thirteen and Amberary, the fourteenth, placed between January and February (Ruby). Counted Ruby’s way, from March, the strip below runs that way, with January, Amberary, February and Tredesember at its end, after the Restart Day.
              Year
              392 days + the Restart Day, which on Hexa is one and a half days long: 393½ days, “same as tetra but probably one month longer”. The year begins on 1 January, after the Restart Day, as on Tetra.
              Years
              Counted from Amber’s landing: “when amber reached cuba, she clled it year one of cuba (so rigt now it is year 50)”, said while Tetra was in 1700. Tetra is in 1750 now (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “the year has advannced to 1750 on tetra (do the math for hexa)”): fifty Tetra years are 18,262½ days, which is 46.4 Hexa years of 393½ days, so it is year 96 of Hexa, about two fifths of the way through it. The page starts both worlds on 1 January together and drops those two fifths of a year: a simplification.
              Week
              Seven days with Tetra’s names: Starday, Moonday, Goldday, Blueday, Spikeday, Wetday, Twilightday (Ruby: “same names for days on cuba also”). 392 month days are 56 weeks, so with the Restart Day outside the week every month runs from a Starday to a Twilightday (a reading, as on Tetra).
              One clock
              Tetra and Hexa share their days: a day here is a day there, and pausing, spinning or stepping time on one does it on both. Their years and months are their own, so when Tetra steps from Tredesember into March, Hexa is just starting Tredesember.
              Amberary
              “half in rain seoson half in transition between rain and spring” (Ruby): the first fourteen days are rain season, the last fourteen the time between rain and spring.
              Seasons
              The rain season runs through the Restart Day, January and the first half of Amberary; then the time between rain and spring; then spring from February. The months from February on have Tetra’s seasons (Ruby, 2026-10-06: “same as tetra”). In the rain season it rains on every side (Ruby), though never on the moon or the star.

                The moon

                “the moon of tetra is similar to cuba” and “a d5 probably” (Ruby). So Hexa’s moon is Tetra’s in every way but the die: a five-sided die, a third of Hexa’s size, circling a little farther out than the magical field, opposite the star on ordinary days, swinging round in front of the star on the 14th of every month for a solar eclipse, rolling once a day, waxing and waning through the month. Ruby first allowed “the round shape used for equal oucomes in the real world, or is just a square piramid”, then wrote “te piramid does not grant equal chances so whatever grants equal chances for bouth moons is good” and “a fair d3 for tetra and a fair d5 for cuba”. Then, 2026-10-11: “Remake the moons without the “barrel” method”. So the d5 is a fair d5 and no barrel: a short five-faced prism, three oblong sides with one, two and three craters and two triangle ends with four and five, proportioned so the five faces come up alike, as the real world’s five-sided die is tuned to be. Which non-barrel shape to use, and the proportion, are readings.

                Life of Hexa

                Ruby: “add most of the recognizable plants from the real world to bouth and add more umbrela tree zinias on cuba than on tetra (cince there is more majic)”, and “anything that grows on tetra also grows on cuba”. So everything that grows on Tetra grows here, most of the plants you would know from Earth among them, for example . The Umbrella Tree Zinnia, whose stem is not wood and whose top is petals, grows here more than on Tetra, since there is more magic. Ruby, 2026-10-06, on which plants grow where: “i don't know yet (earth planets grow all over)”, and 2026-10-14: “tetras and the giant tree”. So Hexa’s plants are Tetra’s plants, growing all over, and the giant tree, the Montezuma; the colours of the land are Tetra’s (“same as tetra”).

                The Montezuma. Ruby: “cuba has a gian tree called montezuma that grow ut to a 15th of the hight of mount celectial”. Then: “it grows to be 1 mile high and 1.5 mile radius in canopy and a 3/4 mile wide trunk it will grow on the east side of cuba when it is writen”. So: a giant tree of Hexa, a mile high, with a canopy a mile and a half in radius and a trunk three quarters of a mile wide, a fifteenth of Tetra’s Mount Celestial by her first line, which she now calls an estimate (below); it will grow on the East side once that side is written, and nothing is drawn until then (the East side is drawn from her sketch since 2026-10-06; whether that is “writen” enough for the tree is hers to say). Ruby, 2026-10-14, on Mount Celestial’s height: “half the night of tetras moon (the the tree was estimating first time, now it's set)”, read as half the height of Tetra’s moon, and the moon’s height taken as its length, after her 2026-10-03 “at least half the length of the moon high” (two readings). So the mountain is set at half the moon’s length (about 4,100 miles, worked out from Tetra’s size, not her number), the fifteenth was her first estimate, and the tree stands at her mile. Ruby, 2026-10-17: “the Montezuma is a kind of tree that so far only grows on hexa”.

                The Plus Continent and the Canyon

                From Ruby’s picture of the Canon side (2026-10-04): a broad island shaped like a cross, with an arm toward the middle of each side and rounded bends at the corners. In the middle she wrote “to far side”: the small hole that takes you to the opposite side of the world. Ruby: “the arms connect to the north south east and west faces”, so the land crosses those four edges; how far it goes on each of those sides is drawn as far as her sketches of the explorers’ maps show, and that is right (Ruby, 2026-10-06: “i don't know yet”; 2026-10-14: “their fine”). The island’s shape is drawn from the description of her picture. Ruby named them: “the hole is called the canyon, the island is called ‘the plus continent’”. And “you can come thugh the hole ither way, so the far side will probably get explored next”.

                How Hexa was reached

                “lets imagine that amber the explorer makes a chamber out of a tree and (calculated corectly) launches of ither spikia or the far side using majic, gets flung by the moving moon (going in or out of solar eclipse) gets flung by the star and lands on the cannon face of cuba (year 1650)”

                Ruby, 2026-10-04, in her words. Amber the explorer, in a chamber made from a tree, launched by magic from Tetra, flung on by the moving moon at an eclipse and then by the star, and landed on the Canon side of Hexa in the year 1650. She launched from Tetra’s Far side (Ruby: “8: far side”).

                The Dice System

                Ruby, 2026-10-10: “We have for planets: a d4 a d6 a d8 a d10 a d12 a d20 a d24 a d30. So 8 planets. Maby make some d0.5’s for asteroids And make a belt? So to recap, tetra, hexa, octo, deca, dodeca, icoso, icosotetra, and triaconta are our planets.” and “Also probably shuld add the d2 and d1 as dwarf planets”.

                  Where the other six sit, in which fields and how far from the star, is unwritten; the d0.5 asteroids and a belt are her question, not built.

                  Key events

                  From Ruby’s comics (2026-10-10): Amber’s flight in Tetra’s year 1650, then the panels she heads C1 to C10, read here as Hexa’s own years (a reading, as her T numbers are read as Tetra’s). Her words as read, (?) where hard to read; what each panel shows is a reading.

                    The explorers

                    Ruby: “5 people also came with amber, they are all explorers: Ammolite, Aquamarine, Axinite, Benitoite, and Chrysoberyl (they are for exploring the other sides when we get there)”. Then: “ammolite has desided to go down the canyon”, and “Ammolite has drawn a map and is heading back down to the cannon side”. Her map is the Far side as drawn here (Ruby, 2026-10-14: “yes”). On 2026-10-06: “North side explored by aquamarine”, “East side discovered by axinite the explorer”, “South side discover by benitoite the explorer”, “Chrysoberyl is waiting until she’s done resting”, “Chrysoberyl’s map of west side”, with her sketches of those four sides, which the sides are now drawn from.

                      Still unwritten

                      • Where the two portals lead after “for now”: Ruby, 2026-10-17, “for now we will make the portals go to each other”.
                      • How much the lands shrink: Ruby said “just shrink them”, not by how much; they are drawn at seven tenths of their size, a reading.

                      Ruby’s answers of 2026-10-14 to the earlier list, in order: the arms’ reach, “their fine”; names, “humands didn't develop there, they don't have any”; which plants grow where, “tetras and the giant tree”; Mount Celestial’s height, “half the night of tetras moon (the the tree was estimating first time, now it's set)”; Ammolite’s map, “yes”, it is the Far side as drawn here. Then, 2026-10-17: “the Montezuma is a kind of tree that so far only grows on hexa”, “yes but dont change the shape, just shrink them” (the lands, for a very watery planet) and “for now we will make the portals go to each other”.

                      The world

                      OCTAThe eight-sided planet · The Dice System

                      The third world of Ruby’s Dice System: the d8, eight triangular sides, turning under the same star with a d7 moon. A ship has landed on Home, side 1; nothing is drawn yet.

                      Sides
                      Eight. Named by the number on the die until 2026-10-18 (Ruby, 2026-10-17: “the sides are just named by the number on the dice”), then by her words of that evening: “pair three fits.witch means 1 is home, 2 is cannon, 3 is west, 4 is south, 5 is north, 6 is east, 7 is far, and 8 is away”. So: Home (1), Canon (2, her “cannon”, spelled as on Tetra and Hexa), West (3), South (4), North (5), East (6), Far (7), Away (8). Home and Away is the pair that joins Hexa’s six (see below); opposite sides add up to 9 and stay paired as Hexa pairs them: Home and Away, Canon and Far, West and East, South and North. With 1, 3, 5 and 7 around the top point and 2, 4, 6 and 8 around the bottom one, Home, West, North and Far make the upper ring and Canon, South, East and Away the lower; how the numbers sit on the die is a reading.
                      Drawn so far
                      Nothing yet. Ruby, 2026-10-17: “so the first side hasent been discoverd or drawn yet”; 2026-10-18: “a ship as landed on side one of octa”. The landing is marked in the middle of side 1 (the spot is a reading); whose ship it is, where it came from and what it found are unwritten. Every side is blank until she draws it. Ruby, 2026-10-18, later again: “maps are being drawn of (what is curently side one) and will be sent to tetra to update the model system soon”. Side 1 will be drawn from those maps when they come.
                      The name
                      Octa, by a vote on 2026-10-17, two to one, and by the rule Ruby gave the same day for every planet: “witchever is the hedron name minus "hedron"”. See below.
                      The star
                      Tetra’s dark purple star, the same for all three worlds (Ruby, 2026-10-17: “give octa the same star”). It stays where it is; turn the world to find it. Where Octa sits among the worlds, and how far from the star, is unwritten, so the star is drawn as large as from Hexa.
                      Turn
                      Octa turns (Ruby: “a turn”): one full turn a day, leftward, like Tetra and Hexa. The direction and the day’s length are readings; its days are the shared clock’s days.
                      Like the others
                      Ruby, 2026-10-18: “EVERYTHING IS SIMILAR TO THE FIRST TWO”. So Octa has the two fields, one magical and one magnetic (the gold and blue rings), rain in the rain season, Tetra’s plants, Tetra’s week, a 25-hour day, and years counted from the ship’s landing as Hexa counts from Amber’s: year 0 of Octa now (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “it shuld be year 0 of octa”). The magical field is stronger than Hexa’s (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “why is octa's magical field the same as hexa, it shuld be stronger”): four gold rings instead of three, thicker and brighter; how much stronger is a reading. The magnetic field is as Hexa’s. Where “similar” had to be read as “the same” (the plants, the week, the day’s length, the magnetic field’s strength, the rain months, counting the years from the landing) it is a reading.
                      The sky
                      Every other planet shows in Octa’s sky (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “you shuld be able to see all of the other planets from a given planet”): Tetra and Hexa as small turning dice nearest the star, the five not yet built as points of light with their names farther along, on one curved line from the star that runs through this world (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “Why are all the planets not in a curved line from te sun”, then: it “was including the planet you are on”, then: “make them in a fixed pint in space that lets it look like they are actualy all in a line and not you are just zoomed in on one planet, engulfing he rest in its fields”), in the order she stacked the fields (2026-10-04: “if there were 5 magical fields, and tetra was in the first one, cuba would be in the last one (going away from the star would be the direction they were stacked in)”): the planets nearer the star stand between it and this world on the screen, the farther ones carry the line on past it. They stand at fixed places in space along that line, outside this world’s fields, so turning and zooming out (the zoom now goes far enough) shows the whole row as it is; a planet hides behind this world or the moon only when it is farther away than they are. The spacing and the bend are readings. She placed only Tetra and Hexa; the page sorts the rest by die size, which puts Octa and the five beyond Hexa: a reading she may overrule. The line’s bend and where it runs across the sky are readings.
                      Unwritten
                      Octa’s size; whose ship landed, which way it lies and what it found; the fifteenth month’s name.

                      The calendar

                      Months
                      15 · 28 days each: Hexa’s fourteen and one more (Ruby, 2026-10-17: “a calender with one more month than hexa”). The fifteenth month sits between March and April and has no name yet (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “the 15th month goes between march and april, but is still unnamed”).
                      Year
                      420 days + the Restart Day, which on Octa is one and three quarters of a day long (Ruby: “a restart day that is one and three fourths of a day”): 421¾ days. The year begins on 1 January, after the Restart Day, as on the other two worlds (a reading).
                      Week
                      Seven days with Tetra’s names, as Hexa has them (a reading for Octa): Starday to Twilightday. 420 month days are exactly 60 weeks, so every month runs Starday to Twilightday and the Restart Day stands outside the week.
                      Seasons and years
                      Like Hexa’s (Ruby: everything is similar): the rain season over the Restart Day, January and the first half of Amberary, then the time between rain and spring, spring from February, summer from April, fall from July, winter from October. The fifteenth month is half and half, as Amberary is (Ruby, 2026-10-18: “the first half of the 15th month is spring, the secont half is in betwee nspring and summer”): spring to its 14th day, the time between spring and summer from its 15th, then summer from April. Years count from the ship’s landing (a reading, as Hexa counts from Amber’s): year 0 of Octa (Ruby: “it shuld be year 0 of octa”). The year before it is -0 and the one before that -1, as Tetra counts its years (a reading).

                      The moon

                      Ruby, 2026-10-17: “a d7 moon”. So Octa’s moon is a seven-faced die, and like the other two moons it is fair and no barrel (Ruby, 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-11): a short five-sided prism with five oblong sides carrying one to five craters and two pentagon ends carrying six and seven, its length picked so each of the seven faces takes a seventh of the view from the middle (the shape and the proportion are readings, as for Hexa’s d5). It is a third of Octa’s size and keeps the other moons’ ways: opposite the star on ordinary days, swinging round in front of the star on the 14th of every month for an eclipse, rolling once a day, waxing and waning through the month. That it keeps those ways is a reading; Ruby gave the die.

                      The name · a vote

                      Ruby, 2026-10-17: “cool now lets add octa (or octo (whichever sounds better (dont just use the first or secont, me, daddy, and you will vote (daddy votes octa, i vote octo)))”.

                      • RubyOcto.
                      • DaddyOcta.
                      • ClaudeOcta, for two reasons. It follows what Ruby did when she renamed Cuba: the planet takes the first half of its hedron’s name (tetrahedron, hexahedron, octahedron), a pattern she has since made the rule for every planet. And Tetra, Hexa, Octa, Deca, Dodeca sound like one family, while Octo pulls toward octopus and October.

                      Result: Octa, two votes to one. Then Ruby made the rule for all of them, 2026-10-17: “witchever is the hedron name minus "hedron"”. So the d20 is Icosa and the d24 Icositetra (icosahedron, icositetrahedron), and the list below says so.

                      The side names

                      Ruby, 2026-10-18, later again: “pair three fits.witch means 1 is home, 2 is cannon, 3 is west, 4 is south, 5 is north, 6 is east, 7 is far, and 8 is away”. Home and Away, the third pair of the last list below, joins Hexa’s six: Home (1), Canon (2), West (3), South (4), North (5), East (6), Far (7), Away (8). The question is answered; the offers below stay for the record.

                      Ruby: “unless you can preduce 2 more directions on top of Hexa's that fit in(give me at least 3 examples before we resort to the numberd situation)”, then “give me another 5 so they arent confusing”, then, 2026-10-18: “for the names, you do not realise that it rotates so that nay face could be seen”. She is right: a side that faces the star now faces away half a day later, so no name tied to the star, the light or the view can stick to a side. Dawn and Dusk, Sunrise and Sunset, Light and Dark, Inner and Outer, Sunward and Starward, Windward and Leeward are withdrawn, and Gold and Blue with them: the gold field lies toward the star and the blue away from it, so those two would move over the sides as well.

                      What does stay fixed on a turning die is its axis: the two points it turns about, and the ring of four sides round each. Hexa’s six are Canon, East, West, Far, North and South. Pairs that stick to the body, none chosen:

                      • Zenith and Nadir: the point on top and the point underneath, the astronomer’s words.
                      • Peak and Deep: the same two points in plain words.
                      • Over and Under: the plainest pair; on Hexa, North is already the top and South the bottom, so these would mean the die’s two points instead.
                      • Crown and Keel: the top of the die and its underside, the way a ship has a keel.
                      • High and Low: the upper ring of four sides and the lower ring of four.
                      • Upper and Lower: the same two rings, said plainly.

                      Ruby, 2026-10-18, later: “can i pleese have 5 more pairs that also dont have anything to do with up and down?” More that stick to the body without its two points (five were offered; two of them are withdrawn below), none chosen:

                      • Hither and Yon: side 1, the ship’s landing, with the three sides that touch it (3, 4 and 7), and side 8 with the three that touch it (2, 5 and 6). Hither is the old word for “this way”, yon for “that way, over there”.
                      • Bow and Stern: the way the ship on side 1 points and the way behind it, as a ship names its ends. Which way the ship lies is hers to say.
                      • Port and Starboard: the ship’s left and right once its bow is set, the sailor’s pair.

                      Odd and Even would be another, but in the page’s layout the odd sides are the upper ring and the even sides the lower, so it would say the same as High and Low unless the numbers move.

                      Ruby, later again: “theese are side names, not directions, and we arent judgeing the greateness of one side to be better than another, pleese coan i have 3 to 5 more pairs?” So Spinward and Counterspin (directions round the die, not names of sides) and Lesser and Greater (one side ranked above another) are withdrawn; Hither and Yon, Bow and Stern and Port and Starboard stay, being names of sides. Five more names for two opposite sides, with nothing of up and down and no side above another, none chosen:

                      • Heads and Tails: the two sides of a coin, which is thrown as a die is; here the ship’s side and the side opposite it, or any opposite pair she picks.
                      • Obverse and Reverse: the same two sides in the coin collector’s words.
                      • Home and Away: the side the ship landed on and the side opposite it, as a team plays at home and away.
                      • Recto and Verso: the front and the back of a page, as a book names its two sides.
                      • Warp and Weft: the two threads of a woven cloth, which cross without either lying over the other.

                      For the record: on an eight-sided die a side is in the upper ring or the lower one, and sits between two of Canon, East, Far and West (Hexa’s six directions are the six corners of this die). So two new words would mark the rings, and a side would be called, for example, the High Canon-East side. If that is not what she means, the numbers stand.

                      The Dice System

                      Ruby, 2026-10-10: “So to recap, tetra, hexa, octo, deca, dodeca, icoso, icosotetra, and triaconta are our planets.” Octa is the third of them to be built.

                        Still unwritten

                        • What is on side 1 beyond the ship’s landing (her maps of side 1 are being drawn and will come), and on every other side; whose ship it is and which way it lies.
                        • The fifteenth month’s name.
                        • Octa’s size, and how far from the star it sits.
                        • The dwarf planets’ names by the hedron rule (a d2 is a dihedron, a d1 has no hedron): hers to say.

                        Octa shares this page with Tetra and Hexa, as Ruby asked for Cuba; the buttons under the title switch between the worlds.
